title: Introduce Helm template transformer and declarative init-graph for private installs
author: Devon Patel
body: Motivation: Private installs exhibit brittle init ordering across cloud/onprem clusters when tenant-scoped seed jobs, cert provisioning and secret reconciliation run concurrently. Existing hook templating duplicates logic in values and templates which makes safe incremental upgrades error prone. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Helm template transformer library (templates/_value_transformer.tpl) that allows environment-aware value morphing and lightweight lookups at render-time, and (2) a declarative initGraph structure surfaced in values.yaml which renders as sequenced Helm hook Jobs and a compact init-graph controller helper that enforces inter-job ordering, per-phase concurrency, and idempotent requeues.  Summary of changes: added values.schema.json for the new valueTransformers and initGraph contract; new helper templates (templates/_value_transformer.tpl, templates/_init_graph_helpers.tpl); an optional preflight dry-run job (templates/preflight-dryrun-job.yaml) that validates transformed values; template overlays for safe rollback (annotations on hook jobs to fence rollback windows); example values at examples/private-values-initgraph.yaml; README updates documenting the new contract and recommended upgrade path.  Checklist: 1) implement transformer helpers and unit tests (done) 2) add values.schema.json and examples (done) 3) update chart README and migration notes (done) 4) run full private-installer e2e with onprem and AWS VPC profiles (green) 5) coordinate rollout with platform team for roll-forward window and feature-flag (deployed behind values.enabled.initGraph).  Backwards compatibility: default values preserve existing behavior when values.enabled.initGraph is false. The transformer DSL is opt-in per-section (valueTransformers.*) so older values continue to render unchanged.  Upgrade notes: Operators should set values.enabled.initGraph=true in a canary tenant first and run preflightDryRun.enabled=true to validate the transformed manifests in-cluster without side effects; the preflight job runs as a non-mutating validation that checks RBAC, CRDs, and image availability. After validation and one successful tenant boot, set the initGraph concurrency to a safe default (1) and ramp up.  Rollback strategy: hook jobs include a rollback-fence annotation and the transformer writes an explicit release-version label; if a rollback is required the hooks will refuse to run against mismatched release-version and an operator can safely revert values.  Testing performed: local helm template checks, values.schema.json validation, integration with private-installer CLI smoke tests, and full e2e in staging using the AWS VPC profile and an on-prem lab cluster.  Risks and mitigations: transformer DSL introduces another templating layer; to limit blast radius it is disabled by default and scope-limited by transformer profiles.  Contact: @devon for rollout coordination and @aisha for operator playbook updates.

release_notes: charts(redwood-private-installer): add opt-in initGraph declarative sequencing and a Helm value transformer DSL. Operators can enable initGraph for safer, ordered tenant bootstrap and use preflightDryRun to validate changes before rollout.
notes_for_ops: Migration steps: 1) deploy chart with values.enabled.initGraph=false to main; 2) pick a canary tenant and set enabled.initGraph=true and preflightDryRun.enabled=true; 3) inspect preflight job logs for transform output and validation errors; 4) if green, set initGraph.phaseConcurrency=1 and continue canary tenants; 5) once stable, ramp phaseConcurrency. Important: ensure all nodes have the required init-image pre-pulled or set images.prepull=true to avoid head-of-line delays. For rollback, use helm rollback and ensure release-version labels match; the init hooks will not run for mismatched release-version, preventing partial double-run.
changelog_entry: Add opt-in Helm value transformer and declarative initGraph to charts/redwood-private-installer (ENH-1729).
safety_notes: Feature is opt-in. Preflight dry-run validates but does not mutate resources. Transformer functions that touch secrets must be gated by 'redact' profiles and are documented in README.
impact_scope: private-installer chart consumers and onprem/vpc operator playbooks
